Mark each cable before you pull it, because once it's out, the mark is the only record of which socket it came from. Ten identical cables don't remember where they lived, and neither will you after strike.

Keep the marks on until everything is plugged back in, because that's how you check the work. The crew compares each reconnected cable with its mark, and a cable sitting in a socket that doesn't match its mark is a swap. Pull the marks early and you've thrown away the only way to catch it before the show finds it for you.

Mark every cable before you unplug it, because the mark records which socket it came out of. Once a cable is loose in a bundle of identical cables, nothing else tells you where it goes, and memory fails exactly when the changeover is rushed.

Leave the marks on until everything is plugged back in and checked. After reconnecting, the crew compares each cable's mark against the socket it actually landed in. That comparison catches swaps: two cables plugged into each other's sockets look fine and may even power up, but send signal or power to the wrong place. Pull the marks early and that check is impossible.
